## Always Opposing

Friction is a force, and every force needs a direction — it isn't a magnitude-only quantity.

Its direction is fixed by one rule: **opposite to the direction of sliding.**

The book slides right, so friction points left, steadily slowing it down. If the book were sliding left instead, friction would point right. **Friction never pushes an object along — it only ever resists whichever way it's already sliding.**
